privacy-section.title: Your activity is not our product
privacy-section.description: What you watch stays on your PC, not on nowly.me.

items.title: Nothing goes through our servers
items.description: Extension, desktop app, then Discord. Title, platform, and playback never leave your PC.

items.title: No analytics unless you ask
items.description: If you turn them on, they only help improve Nowly. You can turn them off at any time.

items.title: Only the sites you install
items.description: A presence runs only after you install it. Remove it, and Nowly leaves that site alone.

faq.title: Questions, answered quickly
faq.description: The essentials on install, data, and Discord. Docs and Discord go further.

items.question: What is Nowly?
items.answer: Nowly shows what you watch, listen to, or play as Discord Rich Presence. It is a browser extension, a desktop app, and a library of platform scripts.

items.question: Does my activity go through your servers?
items.answer: No. Activity stays local and is sent to Discord from your machine. Analytics are optional and off by default.

items.question: Which platforms are supported?
items.answer: The live list is the library. New presences can be added without updating the extension, so install the ones you actually use.

open-source.title: Add a presence
open-source.description: Presence scripts are public. Fork, write, open a PR. The CLI and docs are enough to start.

desktopPage.title: The local bridge to Discord
desktopPage.description: The extension reads the tab. The desktop app sends your status to Discord. Title, platform, and playback never leave your PC.
desktopPage.unsigned-desc: Windows may show a SmartScreen warning. Open More info, then Run anyway, only if you downloaded the file from this page.
desktopPage.signed-desc: macOS builds are notarized. Gatekeeper should accept the disk image.

trust-items.title: Stays on your machine
trust-items.text: The extension sees the tab. The desktop app talks to Discord locally. Nothing is sent to nowly.me.

trust-items.title: Speaks Discord’s language
trust-items.text: Discord only accepts this local bridge. That is why the browser extension is not enough on its own.

trust-items.title: Quiet in the background
trust-items.text: It is small, has no window to babysit, and only runs so your status can update.

guide-items.title: Download the right file
guide-items.text: Use the installer for your system. The portable archive is there if you prefer not to run a setup wizard.

guide-items.title: Open the downloaded file
guide-items.text: Run the app and follow the setup. On Windows, read the SmartScreen note if a protection prompt appears.

guide-items.title: Install a presence
guide-items.text: From the library, add something like YouTube to check that the extension and the desktop app talk to each other.

guide-items.title: Check Discord
guide-items.text: Keep the Discord desktop app open, start a supported site, then check that your status updates.

canaryPage.title: Try the next Nowly
canaryPage.description: Canary is the unpacked build we ship to testers. It moves faster than the stores, and it can break.

card-description.chrome: Chrome cannot install this from the store. You load the unzipped folder yourself.
card-description.firefox: Firefox cannot install this from addons.mozilla.org. You load it as a temporary add-on.

store-note.chrome: Keep the store build for daily use. Canary can sit next to it: they use different extension IDs.
store-note.firefox: Keep the add-on for daily use. A temporary Canary is removed when Firefox restarts.

notes.title: Unstable on purpose
notes.text: These zips track the latest extension work. Features can land, change, or disappear without a store review.

notes.title: No store updates
notes.text: The browser will not auto-update Canary. When a new zip is published, download it again and reload the build.

notes.title: Keep the folder
notes.text: The unpacked or temporary load points at a directory on disk. If you delete or move it, the extension disappears.

chrome.title: Download and unzip
chrome.text: Save the zip, then extract it to a folder you will not throw away after a cleanup.

chrome.title: Open chrome://extensions
chrome.text: Paste that address in the tab bar. Turn on Developer mode in the top right.

chrome.title: Load unpacked
chrome.text: Choose the extracted folder, not the zip. You should see Nowly Canary in the list.

chrome.title: Reload after a new zip
chrome.text: Replace the folder contents with the new build, then hit Reload on the extension card.

firefox.title: Download and unzip
firefox.text: Save the Firefox zip, then extract it to a folder you will keep around.

firefox.title: Open about:debugging
firefox.text: Paste about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox in the address bar.

firefox.title: Load Temporary Add-on
firefox.text: Choose manifest.json inside the extracted folder, not the zip.

firefox.title: Load it again after a restart
firefox.text: Firefox drops temporary add-ons when it quits. After a new zip, replace the folder then load it again.
